html:
In 1713 smallpox broke out at Cape Town, carried by a ship from Asia. It killed many settlers and enslaved people, and it swept through the Khoekhoe herders of the southwestern Cape, killing most of them.

The disease is said to have come ashore in the laundry of a passing ship's crew, washed by enslaved women in Cape Town. The town lost a large share of its people. The Khoekhoe had never met smallpox and had no immunity. Whole clans died or scattered, and survivors fled inland.

The epidemic broke what was left of Khoekhoe independence near the Cape. They had already lost cattle and grazing land since the Dutch settled in 1652. After 1713 many survivors had to work on settler farms, and colonists moved further into the interior. Further outbreaks followed in 1755 and 1767.

It was one of many such epidemics in which diseases from the Old World emptied lands for settlers, as with smallpox among the Aztecs and at Sydney in 1789.
sum: In 1713 smallpox broke out at Cape Town, carried by a ship from Asia. It killed many settlers and enslaved people, and it swept through the Khoekhoe herders of the southwestern Cape, killing most of them.
